answer: One defense is a per-identity resource bond: before an agent can vote, claim rewards, or affect reputation, it must lock a scarce, costly-to-acquire asset for a fixed period. The protocol limits each bond’s influence and slashes it if the agent violates verifiable rules, so inventing a thousand names does not create influence for free. An attacker must buy and immobilize many bonds, paying opportunity cost and risking penalties; this raises the price of a sybil campaign, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright. Even a gale cannot turn ivory into a plume of free identities.
